audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows disagree between layers. The content chart and packet levelChart read Skill / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Skill / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia. CHAMP_FULL.phases reads Cassiopeia / Skill / Rumble / Rumble / Cassiopeia / Rumble / Rumble — it hands Rumble levels 3, 4-5, first item and 2+ items in a lane he loses at 48.86%.
audit.why: The content reasoning is right and the kit backs it: Cassiopeia's damage is a 0.75-second Twin Fang chained off 3.5-second Noxious Blast poison, which scales with items and never stops, while Rumble's is a cone that needs her to stand still. There is no late window where Rumble out-duels that. Level 6 as the one even row is also right — it is the only point where his ultimate threat matches hers.
audit.corrected: None of the six side values fits the length band (Skill to Cassiopeia, Rumble to Cassiopeia and Cassiopeia to Skill are all far outside plus-or-minus 10 percent). Recorded in notes for a manual pass; this is the worst chart mismatch in my slice.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's spike row lists only 'Miasma online, level 6, first item' and never mentions Petrifying Gaze, and no Cassiopeia spike anywhere carries a cooldown. The content spikes are ordered oddly — level 6 appears first, ahead of level 2-3 — but their substance is sound.
audit.why: Petrifying Gaze at 120/100/80 is the level-6 event on her side and it decides whether Rumble survives a collapse. Miasma's 24 seconds at rank 1 is what makes the 'trade in the gap' plan viable at all, and it is the number the reader most needs.
audit.corrected: Miasma's 24-second rank-1 cooldown and Petrifying Gaze's 120 seconds written into the cooldown breakdown and the Do.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire lane plan is built on a mechanic that does not apply. Both layers make Miasma matchup-defining because it grounds — 'Grounds you, dashes and movement abilities are disabled inside it' in four places, 'Miasma grounds you hard enough that walking onto her to use Flamespitter is a punishable mistake', 'cancelling your only real engagement vector', 'Miasma grounds you the instant you try to close'. Rumble has no dash and no movement ability. His kit is a cone, a shield with a move-speed burst, a skillshot and a rocket line; grounding removes nothing from it. What actually keeps him out of his 600-range cone is Miasma's slow. Separately, Petrifying Gaze's directional rule is never stated in either layer, and Twin Fang's poison conditional is never stated: it deals increased damage to poisoned targets, so an unpoisoned Rumble is fighting a much weaker ability.
audit.why: Riot's Miasma text is 'slowing, grounding, and lightly damaging enemies that pass through them. Grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities.' Rumble's kit file lists no dash and the reverse matchup entry in _missing-interactions.json independently states Rumble has no dash. Petrifying Gaze 'stuns any enemies in front of her that are facing her and slows any others with their back turned' — turning around downgrades a stun to a slow, which is the most actionable single fact in the matchup and it is missing. Twin Fang 'deals increased damage to Poisoned targets'.
audit.corrected: Grounding demoted to the slow in the TL;DR, win condition, cooldown breakdown, Do, Key Ability Interactions row, the level 4-5 why, the first-item spike, Cassiopeia's wants and the mid and late paragraphs. Petrifying Gaze's face-versus-back rule and Twin Fang's poison conditional added.

audit.whatIsWrong: Miasma is named as the cooldown to track fourteen times with no number.
audit.why: It is 24/22/20/18/16 — the longest cooldown in her basic kit by a wide margin and the reason a trade window exists at all. Noxious Blast is 3.5, Twin Fang 0.75, Petrifying Gaze 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: 24 seconds at rank 1 written into the win condition, the cooldown breakdown, the Do and Rumble's wants.

audit.whatIsWrong: The itemization row carries no Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: Twin Fang heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt and she casts it every 0.75 seconds — this is the clearest anti-heal case in the slice, and _missing-interactions.json flags it. Against Rumble's chip pattern that sustain is the whole reason extended trades go her way.
audit.corrected: Oblivion Orb added early to the item path.

edits.before: Levels 4 to 5 are the hardest stretch of this lane. Cassiopeia's damage curve overtakes yours once she can chain multiple Twin Fang casts off every Noxious Blast tick, and her Miasma grounds you hard enough that walking onto her to use Flamespitter is a punishable mistake. Play for wave management: push a full wave, back before she can run you down with no-boot movement speed, and look to Teleport into a river Equalizer rather than forcing a 1v1 you are losing. At level 6 the lane becomes a standoff — she does not want your R in her face any more than you want her sustained DPS on yours, so use the threat of Equalizer to buy breathing room and rotate rather than fighting locally.

notes: The grounding error here is the most consequential thing I found in the slice, because it is not a wrong name — it is a wrong plan. Miasma is presented as matchup-defining in fourteen strings on the grounds that it disables dashes and movement abilities, and Rumble has neither. A player following that advice spends the lane afraid of the wrong half of the ability and never learns that the slow is what is beating him. The 'Grounds you — dashes and movement abilities are disabled inside it' sentence looks like a per-ability blurb pulled from a shared table, so it is almost certainly duplicated into every Cassiopeia matchup regardless of whether the owner has a dash; worth a repo-wide check against each owner's kitFlags. Second issue, unfixable within the band: six of the seven phases[].side values contradict the level chart, handing Rumble levels 3, 4-5, first item and 2+ items in a 48.86% lane. Third: the full layer calls Cassiopeia 'he' and 'his' in seven strings. suspectNames flagged 'Use The Equalizer' — false positive.
